cards.text: Moses is talking to Israel, walking them back through their own story. Last time, they marched up to fight without the LORD and got chased off by the Amorites like a swarm of bees (Deuteronomy 1:42-44). Now they turn back toward the wilderness by way of the Red Sea, just as the LORD told Moses.

cards.question: For many days after turning back, where does Israel wander?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses: "You have been wandering around this hill country long enough". Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and I would have paid good money to hear those words!

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses to stop wandering and turn to the ___.

cards.text: Next, Israel will pass through Seir, home of the descendants of Esau, Jacob's twin brother (Genesis 25:24-26). The LORD calls them Israel's brothers, so friend, this isn't a border crossing, it's a family reunion.

cards.question: The LORD says the descendants of Esau will be afraid of Israel.
Esau's people will be afraid of Israel. So what does the LORD tell Israel to be?

cards.text: And the LORD is clear: don't provoke them, and Israel gets none of their land, not even a footprint. That's not "keep off the grass," friend, that's "don't even TOUCH the welcome mat!"

cards.question: Why won't Israel get any of Esau's land?

answers.text: God gave Mount Seir to Esau

cards.question: Israel will need food and water while passing through Seir. How does the LORD say they get it?

answers.text: They pay for it in silver

cards.text: Then Moses stops to remind them. The LORD has blessed all the work of their hands and watched over their journey through this vast wilderness.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD has been with Israel these forty years, and they have lacked ___.

cards.text: So Israel moves on past Seir, turning away from the Arabah road that comes up from Elath and Ezion-geber.

cards.question: After turning away from the Arabah road, which road does Israel travel?

answers.text: The road of the Wilderness of Moab

cards.text: Now Israel is on the road of the Wilderness of Moab. The Moabites are descendants of Lot, Abraham's nephew (Genesis 12:5; 19:36-37), and the LORD has a word for Moses about them.

cards.question: Israel is heading through Moab. What does the LORD tell Moses about the Moabites?

answers.text: Do not provoke them to war
Drive them out of their cities
Ask them to march with you

cards.question: Why won't Israel get any of Moab's land?

answers.text: God gave Ar to Lot's descendants
Moses made a deal with Moab

cards.text: Then Moses drops in a side note: the Emites used to live there, a people great and many, as tall as the Anakites. Yes, THOSE Anakites, from the report that made Israel's hearts melt (Deuteronomy 1:28).
Same kind of history in Seir. The Horites used to live there, but Esau's descendants drove them out and settled in their place.

cards.question: Moses compares Esau's people settling in Seir to something else. What is it?

answers.text: What Israel did in its own land
What Moab did to the Ammonites

cards.text: Back to the LORD's words to Moses: "Now arise and cross over the Brook of Zered." Back at Kadesh, God said go up, and Israel dug in their heels (Deuteronomy 1:21, 26).

cards.question: This time, Israel obeys and crosses the Brook of Zered.

cards.text: Then Moses tallies up the trip from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Zered. Remember the LORD's oath at Kadesh: not one man of that evil generation would see the good land (Deuteronomy 1:35).

cards.question: The trip from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Zered took ___ years.
Why did the trip from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Zered last so long?

answers.text: Until those fighting men had all died
Until the people found the road

cards.text: Moses doesn't soften it. The LORD's hand was against them until every one of those fighting men had died.

Then the LORD tells Moses, "Today you are going to cross the border of Moab at Ar." Thirty-eight years of wandering and now it's TODAY, friend, and I would have had my apron on before He finished the sentence!
Past Moab, Israel's route takes them close to the Ammonites. They're descendants of Lot too (Genesis 19:38), and the LORD has a word about them.

cards.question: The LORD tells Israel to harass and provoke the Ammonites.
What does the LORD say about the Ammonites' land?

answers.text: Israel will get none of it
Israel may take half of it
Israel may buy a piece of it

cards.text: One more side note: Ammon's land was regarded as land of the Rephaim too, a people great and many, as tall as the Anakites. The Ammonites called them Zamzummites, and friend, go ahead and say that out loud, I'll wait.

cards.question: The Zamzummites were great and many. Who destroyed them from before the Ammonites?
Moses says the LORD did the same for Esau's descendants in Seir when He destroyed the Horites.

cards.text: And one last note: the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, were destroyed by the Caphtorites, who came out of Caphtor and settled in their place. That's where we'll pause, friend, because Moses is nowhere near done telling this journey.

findings.problem: Too much of stop 1 depends on discovery guesses rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. Cards 2, 4, 6, 9 and 14 ask for Mount Seir, the direction north, the fear of Esau's descendants, God's reason for withholding their land and the next road without giving the baker a basis to infer those answers. That is five of the stop's eight choices, so this stop becomes more of a guessing game than the allowed occasional discovery question.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Deuteronomy 2:11 is skipped entirely. The baker is never told that the Emites, like the Anakites, were regarded as Rephaim. Besides losing that part of Moses' historical note, this leaves 'land of the Rephaim too' in card 17 without the earlier description that 'too' points back to.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
